_readme: Effect sizes ESTIMATED BY GEMINI from the evidence digest (docs/05) and the full strategy + roadmap. Generated by apps/server/src/estimate-all.ts. The simulator uses these instead of the team priors in pathway_parameters.json (kept there as "team prior" for comparison).

estimates.rationale: Denmark's CPP cut diagnostic waits by 29% (49 to 35d, S14) and Welsh simulation showed ~20d saved across P3-P5 (S24). However, Sweden and Norway only meet fast-track targets in 36-40% of cases (S06, S07). Conservatively scaling by ~40-50% compliance yields ~15-25% reductions in P3-P5 and ~12% in P2 via clearer referral criteria.
estimates.label: Nordic Fast-Track Pathway

estimates.rationale: Non-cancer studies show specialist eConsult responses in <4 days and access waits dropping 17% (63 to 52d in LA County, S15). Applied to lung cancer, rapid specialist advice helps GPs order right workups earlier (cutting ~4d or 10% of 41d in P2) and avoids misdirected referrals (cutting ~2d or 15% of 12d in P3).
estimates.label: GP-Specialist eConsultation

estimates.rationale: Observational studies (S16) show nurse navigators cut referral-to-treatment by 10-19d (21-30% of Finland's 58d P3-P5 total). Because evidence is observational, we apply a conservative ~18-22% reduction across P3-P5 specifically for patients with navigation barriers (living alone, 75+, language barriers) who risk long delays without coordination [ROADMAP p.13, p.32].
estimates.label: Named Nurse Care Navigator

estimates.rationale: A Danish RCT on direct GP access to chest CT found no significant reduction in diagnostic time or stage (intention-to-treat, S17). Furthermore, Finland has the lowest CT density in the Nordics (S02), creating imaging bottlenecks. Following the evidence, we keep the estimated effect near zero.
estimates.label: Direct GP CT Access

estimates.rationale: In Finland, 41% of adults wait >14d for a public GP (S10) and symptom-to-appointment averages 14d vs 2-7d in other Nordics (S02). Expanding the omalääkäri model [ROADMAP p.51] improves trust (modestly trimming P1) and reduces repeat visits before referral, saving ~6d (~15% of 41d) in P2 for public route patients.
estimates.label: Named Family Doctor Continuity

estimates.rationale: Patient delay is >50d (S01), worsened by lung cancer stigma [ROADMAP p.22], lower education (S26), and language/health literacy barriers [ROADMAP p.10, p.33-34]. Roadmap actions 1.3.1-1.3.2 model a national campaign after UK's Be Clear on Cancer. Media campaigns yield modest behavioural shifts, estimated at ~8% (~4.5d of 55d) in P1.
estimates.label: Multilingual Symptom & Anti-Stigma Campaign

estimates.rationale: Living >50km from hospital worsens lung cancer survival (HR 1.47, S18), and distances in Finland reach 400-700km [ROADMAP p.13]. While biopsies and surgery require travel, remote oncology consultations and digital pathways [ROADMAP p.13, p.73] can replace pre-treatment visits and coordinate local testing, cutting ~25-30% of distance-attributable days in P4-P5.
estimates.label: Remote Consultations & Travel Coordination

estimates.rationale: Finnish data (DLBCL proxy, S25; [ROADMAP p.11]) show public primary care takes twice as long to reach referral as private/occupational care (75d vs 35d in P2). Direct fast-track referral criteria for public health centres [ROADMAP p.52] bypass repeat GP visits, conservatively closing about aquarter of public P2 days (~10d of 41d).
estimates.label: Public Primary Care Fast-Lane

estimates.rationale: Out-of-pocket fees and travel costs delay care-seeking and diagnostic testing among low-income/lower-SES patients in Finland (S27, [ROADMAP p.10, p.13]). Organised, reimbursed transport removes financial and logistical travel friction, conservatively cutting 20-25% of distance-attributable delay days in P1, P4, and P5 for lower-SES (basic education) patients.
estimates.label: Reimbursed & Organised Patient Travel
